redEvidence.test: old helper cannot find browserify or its config when tools are hoisted to the workspace root

redEvidence.diagnosedRootCause: packages/bitcore-build/index.js resolves Browserify/Karma/WebdriverIO/Istanbul/Mocha binaries and its own karma.conf.js/wdio.conf.js by concatenating fixed-depth, process.cwd()-relative strings ('./node_modules/@bitpay-labs/bitcore-build/node_modules/.bin/<tool>', falling back to './node_modules/.bin/<tool>'), rather than resolving from the owning package's own location (e.g. __dirname or the module's resolved manifest/bin metadata). This physical-path assumption matches only Lerna's current per-package bootstrap layout, where each consumer gets its own nested 'node_modules/@bitpay-labs/bitcore-build' symlink pointing at a copy of bitcore-build that has its own nested 'node_modules/.bin' with its dependencies. Under npm workspaces, bitcore-build is linked once at the repository root and its dependencies hoist there too, so neither hardcoded depth exists under any consumer directory, even though the tool and the workspace are genuinely installed.
redEvidence.fixtureDesign: Revised after review (see revisionFollowUp below) to be self-contained. A disposable temp directory holds: (1) the helper under test as a byte-for-byte copy of today's real index.js/karma.conf.js, placed inside the fixture at '<fixtureRoot>/node_modules/@bitpay-labs/bitcore-build' with its own minimal package.json -- not a symlink out to the real repository; (2) real npm-style tool packages for browserify/karma/wdio at the fixture root, each with its own package.json 'bin' field and target script, with '<fixtureRoot>/node_modules/.bin/<name>' generated as an npm-style relative symlink from that manifest, not a hand-placed stub; (3) gulp/gulp-rename/gulp-shell/gulp-terser -- the execution engine that runs the helper, not the tool-resolution behavior this task is about -- reused via symlink from the real repository's already-installed copies at packages/bitcore-build/node_modules, since reimplementing a build tool's own dependency tree would not add coverage; (4) a consumer package directory '<fixtureRoot>/packages/consumer' with no node_modules of its own at all. Node's module resolution realpaths through symlinks for cache identity, so the copied helper's own 'require("gulp-shell")' resolves to the same real, cached module object as the test's, letting the test capture the exact command constructed without altering the helper's logic. The unmodified helper content is exercised for real: startGulp('lib', {}) followed by invoking the returned 'browser:uncompressed' gulp-shell task.
